entries.capability: Login submission + success detection
entries.correctedFrom: An earlier diagnosis blamed Enter-key submission as unreliable and switched login() to a button click; that fix failed the same way when the user (not Claude) ran it. The failure screenshot revealed the real bug: a single point-in-time page.url() check right after waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded') races an async/AJAX-driven redirect.
entries.notes: P101_USERNAME/P101_PASSWORD confirmed as the real login field ids on all four apps checked. Root cause fixed by waiting for an actual URL change (page.waitForURL) instead of a single point-in-time check -- that specific fix has NOT been independently re-verified live (credential-based testing is not repeated by Claude itself per this project's own discipline).

supportMatrixRow.verifiedAgainst: Partially verified: live, against FOUR real APEX 26.1 apps (Sample File Upload and Download; Sample Interactive Grids; Sample Charts; the P101_USERNAME/P101_PASSWORD convention held on all four)

entries.capability: Bare page.goto() vs. real UI-click navigation for checksum-protected pages
entries.notes: A plain page.goto() to a friendly URL for a protected, non-public page silently redirects to /login (HTTP 200, not an error), even immediately after a verified login to the exact same page, with or without a session query parameter. A real in-app link click works and stays authenticated. assessNavigationSafety()/navigateViaUiPath() (navigation.ts) formalize this; @apx/testgen emits an unconditional test.skip() for unsafe pages instead of a guaranteed-to-fail goto test. The 'public pages with the same flag are safe' inference is a REASONED INFERENCE (from a different, page-specific HTTP 400 failure mode on p00420), NOT independently live-confirmed -- flagged explicitly as weaker evidence.

entries.capability: Direct friendly-URL GET on a modalDialog page

Root cause (WHY modalDialog pages 400, or how to construct a working dialog-opening navigation context) is NOT diagnosed -- the generator-side symptom is fixed, the underlying capability gap remains. A third page-appearance value, 'nonModalDialog', is confirmed in the EBNF but has zero real instances anywhere in this project's 52+ app local corpus -- this check deliberately does not assume it shares modalDialog's failure mode.

entries.capability: Array parsing when the opening bracket has no inline content on its property line
applications: all 13 real exports parsed at the time of the fix
entries.correctedFrom: REAL, WIDE-REACHING PARSER BUG: parseArray()'s line-advancement logic double-counted the property line's own i++ against its own unconditional first-iteration i++, silently dropping the first array element whenever `foo: [` had nothing inline on the property line. Confirmed present 1550+ times across every real export parsed at the time (templateOptions: [ in exactly this shape) -- #DEFAULT#, almost always the FIRST templateOption, was silently missing from parsed raw bags project-wide the entire time until this fix. This is one of the two wrong-claim precedents ADR-004 cites directly.
entries.notes: Fixed by only advancing i when a chunk was actually consumed (the same guard the closing-bracket branch already used), applied symmetrically to the opening-bracket branch. Regression-guarded with 3 new tests covering bracket-alone, first-token-inline, and single-line array shapes. Verified zero regressions: all 13 real exports still parse/generate with zero warnings, deterministic output, byte-identical against examples/employee-page.

entries.capability: Quoted, space-containing component identifiers (e.g. Interactive Grid row-selector pseudo-column)

entries.notes: Fixed: COMPONENT_OPEN now accepts "[^"]*" as an identifier alternative, unquoted before being stored. Regression-guarded (zero warnings, correct unquoted identifier, region type surviving uncorrupted, trailing button not orphaned) -- confirmed the test fails all four ways on the pre-fix regex.

entries.capability: behavior.target when action = redirectThisApp
entries.correctedFrom: A prior pass claimed 'a full sweep of this project's entire 46+ app real corpus' found ZERO redirectThisApp/redirectOtherApp occurrences -- that was WRONG, and was itself only ever a single-app, single-session grep (ux-pattern-catalog), never the full corpus, even though a sibling evidence string (flow.ts) incorrectly restated it as a full-corpus sweep. Corrected in place (Fourteenth round, QA/Verification Engineer release-gate pass): concurrent-manager has 17 real redirectThisApp occurrences across 12 distinct pages, all three fields (page/items/clearCache) directly witnessed, including a non-literal page value (an item-substitution token).
entries.notes: Confidence raised to 'high' in flow.ts's FLOW_MECHANISM_EVIDENCE per the same bar already used for ApexBranchTarget.url and ApexButton.url (redirectUrl), both also single-app-sourced. redirectOtherApp specifically remains UNWITNESSED in real data -- typed on the same EBNF production/enum symmetry as redirectThisApp only, not independently confirmed (see parser-button-target-redirectotherapp-unwitnessed). Cited production by semantic name (button-behavior-property), not the raw EBNF line number this source file's own comment also carries as supplementary detail -- per DESIGN_GUARDRAILS.md's explicit preference for semantic references over fragile line numbers.

entries.capability: behavior.target when action = redirectOtherApp
entries.notes: Typed on the strength of the EBNF production and the closed 9-value action enum's symmetry with the directly-witnessed redirectThisApp sibling, per ADR-004's parser standard. Zero real occurrences found anywhere in this project's 52+ app corpus as of this pass -- do not claim this is 'confirmed' the way redirectThisApp now is; it is a structural inference from a proven shape, not independently corpus-confirmed.

entries.capability: branch.behavior.target -- real nested-object shape vs. the EBNF's opaque scalar
entries.notes: CONFIRMED EBNF DISCREPANCY (real data wins, ADR-004): branch-a-behavior-property types target as a single opaque scalar with a sibling type enum and flat pageNumber property. Real data never matches this shape -- target is ALWAYS a nested object. page confirmed in THREE distinct shapes: literal number (317/325, dominant), page alias string (customers), item-substitution token (customers). clearCache filed and fixed 2026-08-14 (concurrent-manager, pages/p00351-lookup-manager1.apx:960-968) -- see grammar-assumptions.md 'Still open' resolved entry.

entries.capability: branch component-id presence

entries.capability: validation.type/item/column/error/condition

Runtime validation-failure-display component deliberately DEFERRED, not blocked by this typed field -- see runtime-interactive-grid-validation-mechanism-split for the runtime answer this later resolved.

entries.capability: process.type/point/condition
entries.notes: 1732 real processes across 45/46 apps -- the single highest app-count of any construct typed in this project. Parser-only: no client-JS hook exists to observe which process fired; the resulting page state is already assertable with existing mechanisms.

entries.capability: process.target { tableName/pkColumn/pkItem/returnKeyIntoItem }
entries.ebnfProduction: process (10-group enumeration, no target group defined)
entries.notes: CONFIRMED EBNF GAP: the process production's group-block enumerates exactly 10 groups, none named target -- real data confirms one anyway, common and reproducible on autoRowProcessing/formAutoRowProcessing processes (210 real instances, e.g. customers starter app). Deliberately left untyped -- no concrete diff/coverage consumer has asked for pkColumn/pkItem specifically yet. This is the identified root gap blocking the CRUD-generation discovery pass -- see runtime-crud-generation-discovery-pass-blocked.

entries.capability: computation.itemName/type/condition
entries.notes: 373 real computations across 19/46 apps. CONFIRMED EBNF DISCREPANCY: every computation-a-computation-property alternative marks type 'required' -- real data confirms type can be entirely ABSENT while computation.sqlQuery is present alone (customers starter app); sqlQuerySingleValue is the implicit default in that case, 149/373 real computations show this exact shape. Distinguished, with a caught-and-corrected contamination pass, from the unrelated computation-b (report-column computation) production sharing the same bare component name.

entries.capability: column.link.target -- page/items/clearCache AND the url (external-redirect) variant
entries.correctedFrom: This type's own doc comment previously claimed 'unlike ApexBranchTarget, no external-URL variant is defined anywhere in any column-link production -- a column's link target is always an in-app page redirect.' WRONG -- a real counter-example found (Eleventh round, 2026-08-11): ux-pattern-catalog, pages/p00320-item-detail-full.apx:459-464, column CHILD_RECORD_NAME, the identical `target: { type: url, url: ... }` shape already confirmed for ApexBranchTarget. Before this fix, projectColumn()/projectPageTarget() silently returned an empty/misleading typed linkTarget for URL-redirect columns (the url value itself stayed safe in raw per ADR-001, but the typed field was wrong). Corrected in place 2026-08-12.
entries.notes: Confirmed only ONE real occurrence of the URL-redirect shape in the one directly-accessible corpus app checked this pass -- a real, reproducible finding, not a high-volume one, but the field was empty/wrong for it regardless of frequency.

entries.capability: column.identifier/type/heading/sequence/linkTarget
entries.notes: 10,683 real columns across 39/46 apps -- the single highest-volume construct typed in this project. CONFIRMED EBNF DISCREPANCY: all six productions mark columnName/name 'required' as a body property; 0/10683 real columns ever emit it that way -- the exporter ALWAYS uses the component-id syntax slot instead. Deliberately distinguished from the unrelated chart-internal column (region-chart-property's styling group), checked side by side to avoid conflation.

entries.capability: action.identifier/label/kind/target/url -- distinct from the Dynamic-Action action
entries.notes: 192 real region-nested action instances across 14/46 apps (distinct from the 2211 already-typed Dynamic-Action action variant, action-c -- confirmed genuinely different EBNF parent productions). CONFIRMED IMPLICIT DEFAULT: action-d's type property, marked 'required' in the EBNF, is frequently omitted (169/192) with only label present -- consistent with 'button' being the implicit default, but kept null rather than coerced, since this evidence is narrower than the Chart bar-default precedent.

entries.capability: validation.valueRequired as the canonical 'required' property name
entries.notes: No required flag was observed at all in the original ground-truth app (UX Pattern Catalog) -- requiredness may be template-driven (@/required-floating) or simply a property this app doesn't exercise. validation.valueRequired remains a guess, not confirmed against a real export that actually has a required item re-exported. Needs a hostile fixture app or a real export with a confirmed required field to close.

entries.capability: Top-level APEXlang comments
entries.notes: CONFIRMED real per the official EBNF's <comment> production -- not just an assumption. But zero real occurrences across all 13 (now 52+) real exports parsed -- the ~40 apparent matches found during a check were all false positives (JS/PLSQL comments embedded inside fenced multiline-string code blocks, already correctly captured as opaque text). Deliberately not implemented -- this project builds against real occurrences, not well-specified-but-unencountered ones; the parser would currently emit an 'Unrecognized line' warning for a real one rather than silently misparse.

entries.capability: A property value containing a leading [ / @ or a literal backtick fence
entries.notes: No quoted PROPERTY VALUES have been observed in any real export parsed so far (distinct from the now-resolved quoted-identifier case, parser-quoted-space-containing-identifier-fixed). Needs a hostile fixture app to close.

entries.capability: Tree region as a content/data-display widget
entries.correctedFrom: The type-level classification was corrected in place: previously documented as 'the standard t_TreeNav navigation widget reused as a login picker, not a distinct content pattern' -- THREE genuine CONTENT tree regions were later found (sample-trees, universal-theme-reference, cloud-apps-rest-explorer). Tree IS a real, distinct content pattern -- but the runtime STUB status is unchanged: all three new instances are static-only, zero live ground truth.
entries.notes: Explicit stub, throws UnsupportedComponentError on construction rather than silently guessing an API. Deliberately not built -- no live instance available for any of the 3 confirmed-real content-tree apps.

entries.capability: apex.region(id).widget().calendar(...) runtime API
entries.notes: Static config typed at the parser level (ApexRegion.calendarSettings, see parser-calendar-settings-ebnf-gap) -- 21 real calendar regions in Sample Calendar alone. Runtime component remains explicitly unbuilt: zero LIVE ground truth, none of the three apps with real calendar regions has had a running instance available to check against. Typed metadata does not substitute for verified runtime behavior (ADR-002).

entries.capability: Map region runtime API
entries.notes: Confirmed present in real exports (falls to raw at the parser level -- no dedicated typed field). htmlDomId confirmed set on 11/18 real map regions in sample-maps -- a rich static confirmation of ADR-003's mechanism on this type, but zero live ground truth on the runtime widget itself.

entries.capability: Programmatically firing a named Dynamic Action
entries.notes: No known generic, documented JS API to trigger a named Dynamic Action programmatically -- DAs are bound to specific DOM events on specific components, not individually addressable by name as far as this project has found. Needs research into whether such a capability exists at all before any design.
